rationale: bugs_open/080: the platform's page-creation surfaces used to derive a page's (name, url, page_type) independently, and `pages` is unique on (site_id, name) with NO unique index on url — so a disagreeing identity does not conflict, it INSERTS A SECOND ROW, and both can deploy. This is the exact failure datahelpers.CanonicalisePage's own header says it was written to end. The gap-planner surface was fixed on v1.0.1177; this change finishes the class and adds the missing detection. Measured 2026-08-03 (live DB + wire): robot-hands.com serves TWO live duplicate pairs — /news.html beside /news/index.html with an identical <title> and a self-referential rel=canonical on the stray, and /gripper-catalog.html beside /gripper-catalog/index.html (this second pair is not in the bug file; found by re-keying the census on URL shape instead of page_type, the filter that blinded the original survey). Fleet-wide: 6 collision groups on 2 sites, exactly 2 with two ACTIVE claimants. Remaining un-canonicalised writers measured: create_blog_posts (hand-rolls the identical shape; 0 of the fleet's page names would be altered by canonicalisation, so the change is a no-op for the existing population), deploy_tool (writes <bare>@/tools/<bare>.html where create_tool_component writes tool-<bare>@/tools/<bare>/index.html — concept register TL-010; 12 live legacy-shape rows must NOT be re-keyed or the fix itself mints duplicates, hence the existing-row-aware resolution), create_tool_component's silent flat-URL fallback (080's shape kept alive as an else-branch). adopt_verbatim is deliberately EXEMPT (preserving crawled URLs is its feature; LANDMINES.md records that canonicalising adopted pages is the trap) and gets a fixed-point convergence TEST pinning its hand-maintained name mirror instead. Detection is 080's own fix candidate 3, built as discovery check page_canonical_collision: two grouping signals union-merged (canonical-name catches the /news pair, URL path-key catches /gripper-catalog — measured, each signal alone misses one), files ONE needs_human_review decision item per group only when >=2 claimants are ACTIVE (the bugs_closed/081 idiom — retiring a live page has no mechanism, bugs_open/098 -> RFC_011, and re-typing a shipped row was deliberately declined by 081), suppresses groups a human already ruled wont_fix/rejected (else the same true-in-the-DB collision re-files every sweep for ever), and retracts its own stale open items via the RFC_010 seam. The check mutates nothing. Enablement is a separate image-then-seed step (303) on completeness-discovery-agent; the verifier lockstep obligation (220/302) is included — and note 302 also carries the content_duplication exclusion the 151 lane declared in 220 on 2026-08-01 but never applied live (verified: the live scheduled_tasks.pre_query list has 4 entries, theirs absent), stated loudly in the seed header as a declared catch-up, not a silent sweep-in.

plan.summary: Close the divergent-page-identity class at every creation surface that can safely converge (create_blog_posts, deploy_tool, create_tool_component), pin the deliberately-divergent surface (adopt_verbatim) with a fixed-point convergence test, and add the page_canonical_collision discovery check + verifier so the two live collisions and any future ones become visible decision items instead of silent duplicates. No live row is mutated; enablement is a separate seed applied only after the image is pod-verified.

edits.rationale: 080's fix candidate 3, unbuilt and unclaimed (the phrase appears once in the repo — in 080 itself). Detection is the only honest treatment of the existing damage: retiring a live page has no mechanism (098 veto -> RFC_011) and re-typing a shipped row was declined by 081, so the check files a decision, not a job.
edits.sketch: Two signals per row: canonical name via datahelpers.CanonicalisePage({Role: page_type, Slug: name}) (empty triple and legacy page_type='index' contribute NO signal — the collapse rule would false-collide every such row with the homepage), and URL path-key (strip /index.html|.html; '' -> '/'). Rows union-merged across signals — measured on the live pairs: name-signal alone misses /gripper-catalog, path-signal alone misses nothing today but home-vs-index name collisions exist only in the name signal; one-item-per-signal would file 3 items on robot-hands, not 2. ONE item per merged group, only when >=2 members are status='active'; item_key page_canonical_collision:<shared path-key | sorted canonical names> (order-independent); spec carries path_keys + canonical_names so the verifier can locate the defect (VerifyTarget has no item_key field). Prior wont_fix/rejected under the same key suppresses re-filing (wont_fix releases the dedup slot and the two-strike guard counts only complete/failed — without this arm the same collision re-files every sweep for ever). Open items whose group lost its second claimant are retracted via CheckResult.Resolved (RFC_010 seam). Verifier: re-runs the predicate per signature key; vanished SITE is an error (count=0 would be vacuously resolved), vanished ROWS are the expected fix shape — unlike content_duplication, deletion IS the remedy here.

plan.risks: 1) create_blog_posts: any LLM plan whose post name canonicalises differently now writes a different row than before — measured zero existing rows affected, but a FUTURE re-run of an old plan with a dirty name (spaces/uppercase already handled identically; .html suffix NOW stripped where before it was kept) would upsert a new row instead of colliding with an old dirty-named one; the 0-row measurement says no such row exists. 2) deploy_tool: the either-name lookup adds one SELECT per deploy; if both names exist it prefers the canonical row — that pair is exactly what the new check files for a human. 3) The check is registered but INERT until seed 303 (image->seed order); its items land needs_human_review in a queue with no working surface (bugs_open/033) and promotion of detected items is manual (bugs_open/083) — visible-and-stuck is the designed trade, same as 081. 4) Retraction arm: CheckResult.Resolved closes open page_canonical_collision items when the group loses its second claimant — scoped to this item_type only, exact item_key match. 5) Seed 302 changes the live claim-timeout exclusion via targeted replace() with pre/post assertions; it also carries the 151 lane's declared-but-unapplied content_duplication entry — reviewers should check that carrying another lane's declared entry in a catch-up seed is acceptable; the alternative re-encodes their live gap into the new string. 6) companionGuideIdentity centralises a two-file duplicated sprintf — byte-convergent today, measured; if CanonicalisePage's blog-post arm ever changes, guides move with it, which is the point but is a coupling reviewers should be aware of.
